title: Short Stuff: Can You Not Have A Name?
summary: Short Stuff episode on naming rules: whether you can live without a name (practically no, since names are needed for identification), state and international naming laws (banned numbers, vulgar words, emojis, Nutella-style brand names, fraud-motivated changes; Portugal, Iceland and Denmark approved-name lists), the hospital birth-registration timeline and temporary names like "Baby Girl Smith," California's supplemental name report, the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child right to a name, and the history of middle names (medieval saints' names, World War One military enlistment forms, computer records defaulting to "NMI").
topics: UN Convention on the Rights of the Child
World War One enlistment middle names

segments.title: Opening banter and Detroit name joke
segments.summary: Hosts introduce the short episode on naming and recall past discussion of unusual baby names such as 'Yeah Detroit'.

segments.title: Can you live without a name?
segments.summary: The hosts argue that a person can't realistically get through life without a name, since names are needed for jobs, licenses and other identification.

segments.title: US state naming laws
segments.summary: Naming laws in the US are set by states; about a dozen have none. Common restrictions include numbers (with spelled-out workarounds like 'phr ee' and 'Plan Nine'), vulgar words, Jesus Christ, Adolf Hitler, Santa Claus in some places, Nutella, racial slurs, names used for fraud, and emojis.

segments.title: International naming restrictions
segments.summary: Portugal requires names from an approved list that must be gender appropriate; Iceland and Denmark also reportedly use similar lists.

segments.title: Birth registration and temporary names
segments.summary: Parents must register a birth with a government office, with deadlines varying by state; they do not need a name before leaving the hospital. Hospitals use temporary names such as 'Baby Girl Smith,' and a study suggested 'Jane's girl Smith' reduces mix-ups.

segments.title: Adding a name later in California
segments.summary: Parents who delay naming can file a supplemental name report with the California health department, which has about a year to do so. The hosts cite Kristen Conger's Unlady Like podcast as the source.

segments.title: UN right to a name
segments.summary: The UN Convention on the Rights of the Child says children have a right to a name from birth, with an exception allowing a boy or girl name in extreme circumstances.
topics: UN Convention on the Rights of the Child

segments.title: History of middle names
segments.summary: Middle names began with medieval saints' names, later became non-religious, and were first officially recognized when US military enlistment forms asked for them around World War One. Later computer systems required three name fields, inserting NMI when no middle name was given.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts wrap up the short episode and close with the standard iHeartRadio production credit.
